databaseAssets.name: Hantavirus
databaseAssets.description: Orthohantaviruses are a genus of viruses that includes all hantaviruses known to cause disease in humans. These viruses are primarily maintained in rodent populations, with each hantavirus species typically associated with a specific rodent host. In their natural rodent reservoirs, hantaviruses usually establish persistent infections without causing symptoms. In humans, however, hantavirus infection can result in two serious illnesses: hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS). HFRS is predominantly associated with Old World hantaviruses found in Africa, Asia, and Europe, whereas HPS is primarily caused by New World hantaviruses circulating in the Americas.

databaseAssets.name: HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)
databaseAssets.description: The human immunodeficiency viruses (HIV) are two types of Lentivirus—a subgroup of retroviruses—that infect humans. Over time, HIV leads to acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS), a condition marked by the gradual breakdown of the immune system, making the body vulnerable to life-threatening opportunistic infections and cancers. Without treatment, the average life expectancy after contracting HIV is estimated to be between 9 and 11 years, depending on the specific subtype.

databaseAssets.name: Domestic Cat
databaseAssets.description: The domestic cat (Felis catus), also known as the house cat, is a small carnivorous mammal that has been domesticated. It is the only species within the Felidae family that has been domesticated. Through studies in archaeology and genetics, it has been determined that cats were domesticated in the Near East around 7500 BC. Cats are commonly kept as pets or farm animals but also live independently as feral creatures, often avoiding human interaction. Valued by people for their companionship and their ability to control pests, they are skilled at hunting vermin. With retractable claws designed for capturing small prey like mice and rats, they possess a strong, agile body, quick reflexes, and sharp teeth. Cats are known for their excellent night vision and keen sense of smell. While they are social animals, they hunt alone and are most active during dawn and dusk.

databaseAssets.name: Domestic dog
databaseAssets.description: The dog (Canis familiaris or Canis lupus familiaris) is a domesticated descendant of the gray wolf. Also known as the domestic dog, it was selectively bred from an extinct wolf population during the Late Pleistocene by hunter-gatherers. Dogs were the first species to be domesticated by humans, over 14,000 years ago, even before agriculture emerged. Thanks to their long relationship with humans, dogs have developed the ability to thrive on a starch-rich diet, which would not be suitable for other canid species.

databaseAssets.name: Chorionic Terminal Villus
databaseAssets.description: This functional tissue unit (FTU) illustration includes cell types related to the chorionic terminal villus FTU in the ASCT+B Table Placenta v1.3. Multiple histology atlases, especially Human Microscopic Anatomy (Krstić 1991) and Histology: A Text and Atlas (Wojciech Pawlina and Michael H. Ross 2019) were referenced. Cell type and metrics were primarily defined from (Hu, McDonough, and Layton 2021; Layton and Layton 2019) and (Rasool et al. 2021). Uberon describes this FTU as follows: "The most distal part of a chorionic villus. A chorionic terminal villus is a grape-like structure characterized by a high degree of capillarization and highly dilated sinusoids. databaseAssets.name: Atlantic Salmon
databaseAssets.description: Side view of an Atlantic Salmon. The Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) is a species of ray-finned fish in the family Salmonidae. It is the third largest of the Salmonidae, behind Siberian taimen and Pacific Chinook salmon, growing up to a meter in length. Atlantic salmon are found in the northern Atlantic Ocean and in rivers that flow into it. Most populations are anadromous, hatching in streams and rivers but moving out to sea as they grow where they mature, after which the adults seasonally move upstream again to spawn

Uberon describes this FTU as follows: "The basic functional unit of the kidney. Its functions are vital to life and are regulated by the endocrine system by hormones such as antidiuretic hormone, aldosterone, and parathyroid hormone." databaseAssets.name: Domestic Cat
databaseAssets.description: The domestic cat (Felis catus), also known as the house cat, is a small carnivorous mammal that has been domesticated. It is the only species within the Felidae family that has been domesticated. Through studies in archaeology and genetics, it has been determined that cats were domesticated in the Near East around 7500 BC. Cats are commonly kept as pets or farm animals but also live independently as feral creatures, often avoiding human interaction. Valued by people for their companionship and their ability to control pests, they are skilled at hunting vermin. With retractable claws designed for capturing small prey like mice and rats, they possess a strong, agile body, quick reflexes, and sharp teeth. Cats are known for their excellent night vision and keen sense of smell. While they are social animals, they hunt alone and are most active during dawn and dusk.

{"officialCategories":["Viruses"],"officialSubcategories":["Enveloped","Enveloped DNA Virus","Enveloped RNA Virus","Reverse Transcribing"],"collection":"NIAID Visual & Medical Arts","creationDate":"6/1/2026","submissionDate":"6/1/2026","modificationDate":"6/1/2026","author":"Ryan Kissinger","sourceUrl":"https://bioart.niaid.nih.gov/bioart/682","name":"Hantavirus","subcategory":"Enveloped","width":500,"height":500,"palette":["#d1d1d1","#8a8a8a","#424242","#afafaf","#848484","#9c9c9c"],"elements":410,"vectorElements":336,"originalFilename":"Hantavirus0001-BW.svg","source":"/Users/ardaodabas/Desktop/scientific-figure-editor/data/bioart-source","category":"Viruses","tags":["Andes","Bunyavirales","cardiopulmonary syndrome","hanta","Hantaviridae","Orthohantavirus","RNA virus","zoonotic"],"description":"Orthohantaviruses are a genus of viruses that includes all hantaviruses known to cause disease in humans. These viruses are primarily maintained in rodent populations, with each hantavirus species typically associated with a specific rodent host. In their natural rodent reservoirs, hantaviruses usually establish persistent infections without causing symptoms.
